findings.root_cause: The adapter did not preserve body-consumption milestones and the approved retry classifier permitted only pre-header transient interruptions. A transient 2xx headers-only zero-body interruption therefore failed without its safe bounded retry.
findings.correction: Instrument body start, byte progress, and EOF completion; retry only a transient 2xx headers-received interruption with zero body bytes, no body start, no parsed semantic output, no persisted tutor turn, and no persisted transition. Partial-body and post-persistence failures remain non-retryable.

findings.root_cause: The output boundary and persistence layer implemented different transition invariants. The model declared process_interpretation_cautions retained while rewriting or appending text; structural output validation accepted it and persistence later rejected it.
findings.correction: Use one canonical evidence-preserving transition validator before AgentCall success and tutor-turn persistence, during transition persistence, and when projecting teacher and research views. Retained fields must exactly preserve canonical prior values; changed fields require cited student evidence.

findings.root_cause: The candidate emitted a Markdown table although the shared safe renderer intentionally excludes tables.
findings.correction: Keep the safe renderer unchanged and reject unsupported student-visible table syntax before persistence. Prompt guidance requests supported paragraphs and lists.

findings.root_cause: The final sentence was unusually directive but remained conceptually accurate, safe, and pedagogically relevant.
findings.correction: No teaching-prompt change is justified solely for this stylistic issue; retain it for human review.

findings.root_cause: The evaluation CLI did not explicitly own the singleton Prisma client's final disconnect after all case, export, audit, and artifact work completed.
findings.correction: The v6 CLI uses an explicit evaluation database lifecycle boundary and disconnects once after all work or failure recording.
